name: Azure Fess
description: Azure Fess is a world of unbroken ocean, its surface a single body of water stretching from pole to pole without a single landmass breaking the horizon. The ocean's color shifts from deep cobalt in the tropics to pale cerulean near the poles, bisected by a darker band of deep water along the equator that gives the planet its heraldic name. Perpetual storm systems churn across the temperate zones, their lightning illuminating waters that glow with bioluminescent life for kilometers in every direction.

The sound of Azure Fess is the sound of water in all its moods: the crash of waves against the research platform's pylons, the hiss of rain on the open sea, the deep subsonic groans of pressure shifts in the abyssal layers below. The air is thick with salt and moisture, and visibility shifts from crystalline clarity to impenetrable fog within minutes. At night, the ocean becomes a mirror of shifting blue light as vast shoals of luminous organisms rise from the depths to feed.

Beneath the surface ocean lies a second, separated by a kilometers-thick layer of compressed ice formed under extreme pressure. This subterranean ocean, warmed by geothermal vents, harbors an ecosystem entirely distinct from the surface waters. The research outpost, a floating platform anchored to a deep-sea ridge, has cataloged over forty thousand species in the upper ocean alone, with the lower ocean still largely unexplored.

Azure Fess's medicinal compounds, harvested from deep-water organisms, have proven effective against several previously untreatable conditions, making the planet a pharmaceutical frontier. The dual-ocean structure presents a scientific mystery of the first order, as the mechanisms maintaining the pressure ice barrier are not fully understood. Recent sonar surveys have detected regular geometric patterns in the lower ocean's floor topology, suggesting either extraordinary geological coincidence or something far more intentional.
